name: SOUL
fullName: Oral Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in High-Risk Type 2 Diabetes (SOUL)
population: n=9650, 50 years or older, NIHSS not applicable — enrolment by vascular and renal risk, not stroke severity, mean follow-up 47.5 ± 10.9 months; median 49.5 months
finding: MET superiority: 579 of 4825 (12.0%; 3.1 events per 100 person-years) with oral semaglutide vs 668 of 4825 (13.8%; 3.7 per 100 person-years) with placebo
teachingPoint: Establishes that an oral GLP-1 receptor agonist reduces major adverse cardiovascular events in high-risk type 2 diabetes, giving a tablet option for vascular risk reduction where injection is a barrier.

name: SURPASS-CVOT
fullName: Cardiovascular Outcomes with Tirzepatide versus Dulaglutide in Type 2 Diabetes (SURPASS-CVOT)
population: n=13165, mean 64.1 ± 8.8 years; 29.0% women, NIHSS not applicable — enrolment by diabetes and atherosclerotic disease status, event-driven; follow-up duration not stated in the abstract
finding: MET non-inferiority but DID NOT meet superiority: 801 events (12.2%) with tirzepatide vs 862 (13.1%) with dulaglutide
teachingPoint: Caps expectations for incretin therapy: tirzepatide matched but did not beat dulaglutide on cardiovascular events, so agent choice within the class should turn on glycemic, weight, tolerability and access considerations rather than on an assumed cardiovascular advantage.
